newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian bourse makes moves to improve trading.
newsitem.headline: Croatian bourse makes moves to improve trading.

text.p: Croatia's central bourse, the Zagreb stock exchange, said on Friday it was developing a new system to enable on-line trading on the country's growing share-market.
Its spokesman Zeljko Kardum told reporters during an annual bourse conference that moves were also being made in cooperation with brokers to speed up somewhat lagging settlement and share transfer.
"This is in the interest of both brokers and bourse, and investors," he said. "It is the most we can do since we cannot push for the development of legislation," he said.
Although it has a very quick payments' system, settlement in Croatia is seven days after each transaction, but traders say it sometimes takes even longer.
According to the current company law, each firm is in charge of keeping the shareholder register and traders complain some of them take inexcusably long to effect share transfer.

A proposed dematerialisation of securities and forming of a central depositary would speed things up considerably. But like with the securities commission, its establishment has been delayed for months now.

"Unfortunately we can influence only those companies (whose shares) are listed in the first and second stock bracket," Kardum said, adding that the bourse had delisted electronic car parts maker Elcon from the second tier from October 1.
He said between three and five more firms might meet requirements for the listing in top bracket by the end of March next year, although none have yet submitted a formal request for it.
Croatia Airlines has asked for its listing to be upgraded to the second tier.

The bourse also has a semi-regulated segment with a number of active stocks. All trading is done off-line at a danger of serious overloading or even breakdowns in case the already high number of transactions shoots up, Kardum said.

The bourse's head of trading Davorin Rusevljan said the entire project of establishing direct links between 45 member brokerages and the Zagreb stock exchange, to begin from January 1 next year, would require some 1.25 million German marks.

But he said the actual cost for each of them, estimated at 40,000 kuna including additional equipment, was bound to pay off because of the increased trading potential enabled by the new system. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
